text: An army marched into the desert to kill one man. The desert swallowed it. Weeks earlier, he was just a man in a quiet city, giving away gold without counting. People began to whisper that he was the one the prophet had promised. A man from the prophet's own family who would fill the earth with justice as it had been filled with oppression. He never claimed it. He ran. He fled to the one place no army should ever touch, the Sacred House in Mecca. But the men who feared him sent an army after him. Soldiers, trucks, armor, a column longer than the horizon. Fourteen centuries ago, the prophet said a man would seek refuge in the house. An army would be sent against him, and when it reached open ground, the earth would swallow it. Then the sand began to tremble, and the ground opened. By morning, there was only flat sand and tire tracks that led nowhere. In Mecca, a hundred thousand hands reached toward the man who had run, and far to the north, an empire signed a peace treaty it never meant to keep.
